sources.entry: _Libraries for machine learning. Also see awesome-machine-learning._

summary.one_liner: A curated, language-organized list of machine learning frameworks, libraries and software, with entries grouped by programming language and subject area.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome" list rather than a software project: it links to ML frameworks, libraries and tools, organized by programming language (C, C++, Python, Go, Java, JavaScript, R, Rust and many others). Under each language, entries are grouped into subject headings such as General-Purpose Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Natural Language Processing, Speech Recognition, Deep Learning, and Data Analysis / Data Visualization. Each entry is a one-line description, and entries marked [Deprecated] are flagged as no longer maintained. The README also points to separate lists for free ML books, courses, events, blogs and meetups. The README states that entries should be removed if their owners say they are unmaintained or they have not been committed to for 2 to 3 years. The README is truncated, so the Python and later sections were not visible.
use_cases: find a machine learning library for a specific programming language
compare deep learning frameworks by language
identify deprecated ML projects to avoid
notable: Organized by programming language, then by subject area
Marks abandoned projects with a [Deprecated] tag
Links to companion lists for books, courses, events, blogs and meetups
Inspired by awesome-php, per the README
caveats: The README says PRs are restricted: contributors must email the maintainer to prove they are human before a PR is merged
Entries can be stale; the README itself says libraries should be removed after 2 to 3 years without commits
The README is truncated, so not every section was visible
